elements.element: Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: 11.1.1.3(a): "PB shall be the exclusive and sole owner of, and retain all right, title and interest in and to, all Trial Inventions ... regardless of inventorship"; as amended, 11.1.1.4: "PB shall be the sole and exclusive owner of the Trial Data Package including the Research Results".

elements.element: Vendor assigns the Deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: 11.1.1.3(a): "SFJ, for itself and on behalf of its Affiliates, hereby assigns ... to PB all its right, title and interest in and to Trial Inventions"; amended 11.1.1.4: "SFJ hereby assigns and transfers to PB all right, title and interest it may have in the Trial Data Package"; 14.3.1 backstop assignment retained.

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: 11.1.1.1: "each Party will retain all right, title and interest in, to and under all Intellectual Property that is Controlled by such Party as of the Effective Date."

elements.element: Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: No licence-back of SFJ pre-existing IP embedded in Trial Inventions or the Trial Data Package appears anywhere in the rendered language; 11.1.1.1 simply reserves each Party's existing IP with no grant to PB. To reach the preferred level the drafter would have to insert an express perpetual licence to any SFJ IP embedded in the Trial Inventions/Trial Data Package.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: No embedded-IP licence exists at all, so no irrevocability wording is present; the only "irrevocable-equivalent" language (exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free, fully-paid licences in 11.1.1.3(b)/(c)) concerns consultants' and Third Party contractors' rights in Trial Inventions, not SFJ's own background IP.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: No grant of SFJ background IP to PB is rendered, so there is no royalty-free characterisation of any embedded-IP licence.

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: Amended 11.1.1.4 first sentence vests the Trial Data Package (all Information generated in the Clinical Trials) and Research Results in PB as "sole and exclusive owner"; the former SFJ ownership sentence is gone and the deterministic check "no assignment of Customer Data/IP to Vendor remains" passed.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: Amended 11.1.1.4: "SFJ may process them solely to perform its obligations hereunder" — a single-purpose service-delivery limitation with no resale, exploitation or "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" tail.

elements.element: The parties do not jointly own intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Ownership is allocated unilaterally throughout: PB sole owner of Trial Inventions "regardless of inventorship", PB sole owner of the Trial Data Package as amended, and each Party retains its own pre-Effective Date IP (11.1.1.1). No joint-ownership language appears.

elements.element: Vendor may retain ownership of generic tools and know-how.
elements.evidence: 11.1.1.1 preserves SFJ's pre-existing Intellectual Property (which by definition includes know-how, methods and trade secrets Controlled as of the Effective Date); the redline does not touch this favourable retained provision.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply in the licence form because PB takes outright ownership: 11.1.1.3(a) makes PB "the exclusive and sole owner of, and retain all right, title and interest in and to, all Trial Inventions", and amended 11.1.1.4 makes PB sole owner of the Trial Data Package — a permanent right that exceeds a perpetual licence.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: Ownership is transferred by present assignment ("hereby assigns" in 11.1.1.3(a) and amended 11.1.1.4, with the 14.3.1 backstop), leaving SFJ no revocation or claw-back mechanic; the former buy-back/re-sale structure has been removed.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is worldwide.
elements.evidence: Title vests in PB without territorial limit ("all right, title and interest"), and the flow-through grants SFJ must obtain from consultants/contractors are expressly "exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free, fully-paid, freely-assignable" (11.1.1.3(b), (c)).

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: No royalty or ongoing usage fee is imposed on PB's use of Trial Inventions or the Trial Data Package; the flow-through licences are "royalty-free, fully-paid". The retained [***] consideration and Approval Payments are one-off transfer consideration, not a use royalty.

elements.element: Customer may use and modify Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: As sole owner of Trial Inventions and (as amended) the Trial Data Package/Research Results, PB may use and modify them without restriction; no field-of-use or use restriction on PB is retained anywhere in the rendered text.

elements.element: Customer may sublicense Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: Ownership carries the right to license; in addition the contractor/consultant grants run to PB "with the right to sublicense through multiple tiers" (11.1.1.3(b), (c)).

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: Amended 11.1.1.4: "SFJ may process them solely to perform its obligations hereunder" — SFJ's obligations are the conduct/funding of the Development Program, i.e. service delivery; no distribution, resale or independent-exploitation right survives.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: Same operative sentence in amended 11.1.1.4 satisfies this element at both levels.

reasons: Position-complete at the fallback level: every fallback element is met by the amended Section 11.1.1.4 read with the untouched Sections 11.1.1.1 and 11.1.1.3, which already give PB outright ownership of Trial Inventions and preserve each Party's background IP.

The preferred level is not reached solely because no licence-back of SFJ background IP embedded in the Trial Inventions/Trial Data Package exists anywhere in the operative text. If the preferred position is wanted, insert one sentence: 'To the extent any SFJ Intellectual Property Controlled as of the Effective Date is embedded in or necessary to use the Trial Inventions or Trial Data Package, SFJ grants PB a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to use it for such purpose.'

The walk-away trigger is cured in operative language, not merely in the comment: the sentence vesting the Trial Data Package in SFJ is deleted, PB is declared sole and exclusive owner, and SFJ's rights are cut back to processing 'solely to perform its obligations hereunder'. The deterministic check that no assignment of Customer Data to Vendor remains is confirmed on inspection.

Minimality holds: edits are confined to the three sentences of 11.1.1.4 that carried the reversed ownership; the [***] consideration, the Approval Payments hook, the Exhibit K entry obligation and the 14.3.1 backstop assignment are all retained, and no survival tail, expense, remedy or procedural extras were added.

Residual conforming point (not fatal, but worth closing): Section 6.1 still describes the payment as being 'In exchange for the purchase of the Trial Data Package as set forth in Section 11.1.1.4', and Exhibit K remains styled the 'Trial Data Package Purchase Agreement'. The amended 11.1.1.4 still transfers title for stated consideration, so the payment basis is not left dangling, but we should either conform 6.1 to 'In consideration of the assignment of the Trial Data Package under Section 11.1.1.4' or confirm the Exhibit K form is amended so its purchase/sale mechanics do not contradict PB's declared existing ownership.

Also consider tightening the second sentence, which now reads as a quitclaim ('all right, title and interest it may have') sitting alongside the first sentence's declaration that PB is already sole owner; this is standard belt-and-braces drafting and is internally workable, but SFJ may argue the quitclaim implies SFJ held title first.
